# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–9 (Complete – Updated 88)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; **spring of third year (present narrative through auction and financial crisis)** (narrative extends into future years); present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village, Bloomsbury, Harrowgate, parsonage, forge, Brompton, barracks neighbourhood, City church, Gloster Coffee House, Portsmouth, Threadneedle Street, Fulham Road, St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), Provence, Elba, Notre Dame, Stock Exchange, Russell Square, Coldcombe hill farms, Salford granary

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist
- **Secret Marriage**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church by special license
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Living with Rawdon in snug little Brompton lodgings; wearing new gloves, shawls, rings, watch purchased by Rawdon; marriage revealed through letter found on pincushion by Miss Briggs
- **Piano Situation**: Discontented with hired piano; attempted to purchase small square piano at Russell Square auction (former instrument from Amelia Sedley's sitting-room); bid unsuccessful as Captain Dobbin's agent (operating for Dobbin's benefit to Amelia) outbid her
- **Contact with Miss Crawley**: Controlled household access at Park Lane; read Morning Post to Miss Crawley; now denied access as door kept by Mr. Bowls; letters sent back unopened

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church by special license
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Living with Rebecca in Brompton lodgings furnished luxuriously; awaiting Miss Crawley's recovery; anxiously considers possibility she may not recover (potential loss of fifty thousand pounds inheritance); denied door access by Mr. Bowls; servants cannot gain lodgment in Park Lane house; letters unopened
- **Financial Strain**: Household suffers from lack of ready money; reads Gazette; discovered Lieutenant G. Osborne promoted to Captain by purchase (vice Smith); this news prompted visit to Russell Square regarding Osborne
- **Debt Note**: Played billiards at Cocoa-Tree, won two hundred pounds from George Osborne

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- **Response to Marriage Revelation**: Gave final scream and fainted upon learning Rebecca married to Rawdon; suffered one fit of hysterics succeeding another; doctor and apothecary summoned; confined to bed under care of Mrs. Bute Crawley as nurse
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: "Long in coming-to"; month has elapsed since revelation; never stirs out, unwell; door kept by Mr. Bowls; access denied to Rawdon and Rebecca; letters sent back unopened; remains under Mrs. Bute's continued presence

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; arrived at Park Lane by Portsmouth mail morning of marriage revelation crisis
- **Actions and Positioning**: Declared Rebecca "artful little hussy"; considered Rawdon profligate; positioned herself as nurse to Miss Crawley; took vacant room at Park Lane to attend her; remains present continuously; guards access to Miss Crawley; has not left her side; characterized by Crawley couple as source of "evil auguries"

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul; confirmed engagement to George; completely innocent of broader events; trusts George completely
- **Emotional State and Isolation**: Currently ailing and low-spirited; went to her room early; lying awake and unhappy overhead while parents discuss family ruin; isolated despite being surrounded by family and friends; has no true confidante; cannot confess doubts and cares to mother; finds would-be sisters increasingly strange; harbors secret misgivings and fears about George she dare not acknowledge even to herself
- **Feelings About George**: Heart tries to persist in asserting George is worthy and faithful, though she knows otherwise; experiences many unanswered things said to him; endures daily suspicions of his selfishness and indifference which she obstinately overcomes; too modest, tender, trustful, and weak to recall her heart once given; pure bashful maiden unable to admit George is her inferior; suffers daily struggles and tortures in silence; hero himself only half understands her
- **Financial Crisis**: Father John Sedley ruined; name proclaimed as defaulter on Stock Exchange; bankruptcy and commercial extermination followed; forced to hide head with wife and parents at St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), small cottage near Fulham Road (recent change in status)
- **Piano**: Owned small square piano (now sold at auction) formerly in sitting-room at Russell Square; instrument acquired by Captain Dobbin for her benefit

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; now ruined man; proclaimed defaulter on Stock Exchange; declared bankrupt and commercially exterminated
- **Collapse Details**: All ventures failed; merchants broke; funds behaved unexpectedly; kept sad counsel about troubles
- **Crisis and Revelation**: Came home very late from City; upon news of ruin, sprang up to meet wife with hasty voice announcing "We're ruined, Mary. We've got the world to begin over again, dear. It's best that you should know all, and at once"; trembled in every limb and almost fell; appeared most moved by shock despite expectation wife would be overpowered
- **Emotional Experience**: Opened pent-up soul during long night, telling story of losses, embarrassments, treason of oldest friends, and unexpected kindness from unexpected sources; gave general confession; moved by wife's faithful response; his heart uplifted and cheered by her consolation
- **Aging**: In six weeks aged more than in previous fifteen years due to harassment from creditors
- **Servants and Household Dissolution**: Discharged wages of domestic establishment with punctuality; servants departed to better positions without breaking hearts; Amelia's maid resigned to better herself in genteeler quarter; Black Sambo determined to set up public-house; old Mrs. Blenkinsop (who witnessed birth of Jos and Amelia, wooing of John and Mary) alone offered to stay without wages, having amassed considerable sum in service, and accompanied family to St. Adelaide Villas where she tended them and grumbled

**Mrs. Sedley (Mary)** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's mother; initially writing cards for a party, unaware of financial ruin; prattling about George Osborne's neglect, Edward Dale's apparent interest in Amelia, and Captain Dobbin's likely interest
- **Response to Ruin**: Upon learning of bankruptcy from husband, ran to him crying; he seized her in arms; took office of consoler when he sank back; took his trembling hand, kissed it, put it round her neck; called him "her John," "her dear John," "her old man," "her kind old man"; poured out hundred words of incoherent love and tenderness; faithful voice and simple caresses wrought his sad heart with inexpressible delight and anguish, cheering and solacing his overburdened soul
- **Current Status**: Living in reduced circumstances at St. Adelaide Villas; present during night of husband's confession

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports; adored by men; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Engagement**: Engaged to Amelia; furious upon learning regiment knows; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"
- **Status Change**: Promoted from Lieutenant to Captain by purchase (vice Smith, who exchanges); announcement read in Gazette
- **Neglect of Amelia**: Not visited recently; has been in town twice without calling on Amelia; seen at Opera by Edward Dale; girls (his sisters) have not been in Sedley house three weeks
- **As Debtor Situation**: According to Mrs. Sedley, has become "such a dandy" with "military airs"; mother views him with impatience regarding his neglect of Amelia
- **Debt with Rawdon**: Won two hundred pounds from Rawdon at billiards at Cocoa-Tree

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER - INTRODUCED]
- Wealthy merchant; old friend and neighbor of John Sedley; George Osborne's father
- **Past Relationship with Sedley**: Sedley set him up in life; Osborne under hundred obligations to Sedley; his son George to marry Sedley's daughter
- **Current Opposition**: Most determined and obstinate opponent of Sedley in creditor debates; harassed Sedley severely; bitterness of opposition inexplicable given past obligations and family connection
- **Character Analysis - Narrative Commentary**: When man has been under remarkable obligations to another with whom he subsequently quarrels, common sense of decency makes former much severer enemy than mere stranger; persecutor bound to prove fallen man is villain to account for own hard-heartedness, ingratitude, and selfishness; from mere sense of consistency, must show fallen man is wretch—otherwise persecutor himself is wretch
- **Butler**: Purchased port wine for Osborne's cellar from Sedley's sale

**Captain William Dobbin** [CHARACTER]
- Carried off George Osborne from billiards; cannot play piano nor dance on tight rope
- **Action at Auction**: Served as agent bidding for small square piano at Russell Square auction; successfully outbid Rawdon's agent; acquired piano for Amelia Sedley's benefit; aware of and responding to Sedley family's distress

**Other Characters**
- **Miss Briggs**: Found letter on Rebecca's pincushion containing marriage revelation early morning; read "affecting and interesting document"; reinstated as first confidante of Miss Crawley; reported intelligence of clandestine marriage to Mrs. Bute upon arrival
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; now widower; made marriage proposal to Rebecca; upon learning marriage, broke out into fury; became frenzied old man, wild with hatred and insane with baffled desire; ransacked Rebecca's room at Queen's Crawley, destroying her belongings (few days after Lady Crawley's burial)
- **Lady Crawley**: Deceased; Sir Pitt's wife; died during winter at Wilhaven
- **Mrs. Firkin**: Witnessed proposal with Miss Briggs; oversees servants at Park Lane
- **Miss Horrocks**: Butler's daughter at Queen's Crawley; took some of Rebecca's relics from boxes Sir Pitt flung open
- **Mr. Bowls**: Doorkeeper at Park Lane; denies Rawdon and Rebecca access; returns their letters unopened
- **Mr. Clapp**: Clerk of Mr. Sedley; found domicile at St. Adelaide Villas with Sedley family
- **Black Sambo**: Servant; determined on setting up public-house after Sedley discharge
- **Mrs. Blenkinsop**: Old servant; witnessed birth of Jos and Amelia, wooing of John and Mary Sedley; amassed considerable sum in service; staying with Sedley family at St. Adelaide Villas without wages; tends them and grumbles
- **Amelia's maid**: Profuse in condolences; went off resigned to better herself in genteeler quarter
- **Edward Dale**: Young stockbroker; saw George at Opera; Mrs. Sedley believes he would marry Amelia if encouraged; member of Messrs. Dale, Spiggot, and Dale of Threadneedle Street
- **Mr. Hammerdown**: Auctioneer at Russell Square auction
- **Mr. Lewis**: Purchased small square piano at auction (agent of Captain Dobbin)
- **Seena Orlwood**: Went to live in Gulton
- **Colan, Movie, Cotho Hollwood, Orrine Stenworth, Colan Lindson**: Secondary characters with minor narrative presence observing local events; Colan Lindson's wife died of coughing sickness summer; Cotho Hollwood told Orrine Stenworth fire at Salford granary was set on purpose

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)
- **MARRIAGE REVELATION OCCURRED**: Rebecca's secret marriage to Rawdon discovered through letter found on pincushion by Miss Briggs
- **MISS CRAWLEY'S CRISIS**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed under Mrs. Bute's continuous nursing; month elapsed; not "coming-to"; never stirs out
- **ACCESS DENIAL**: Mr. Bowls prevents Rawdon and Rebecca entry to Park Lane; their letters returned unopened; Mrs. Bute remains continuously present
- **SEDLEY BANKRUPTCY**: John Sedley declared defaulter on Stock Exchange; bills protested; act of bankruptcy formal; house and furniture of Russell Square seized and sold up; family thrust to hide at St. Adelaide Villas
- **SEDLEY FAMILY DISSOLUTION**: Servants discharged; only Mrs. Blenkinsop remained; family reduced to humble circumstances; John Sedley aged visibly under creditor harassment; wife proved most faithful consoler
- **JOHN OSBORNE'S OPPOSITION**: Most determined creditor opposition comes from George's father, Old Mr. Osborne, despite past obligations and family connection; narrative commentary on how beneficiary becomes severest enemy to justify own ingratitude
- **AMELIA'S ISOLATION AND SUFFERING**: Ailing and low-spirited; lying awake unhappy overhead during family crisis; isolated despite family presence; no true confidante; secretly harbors doubts about George's faithfulness; endures daily suspicions of selfishness and indifference; too tender and trustful to admit or recall heart given to unworthy man; hero himself only half understands her
- **GEORGE'S NEGLECT**: Not visiting Amelia; twice in town without calling; seen at Opera; his sisters absent from Sedley house three weeks; becoming dandy with military airs
- **NARRATIVE CONTEXT**: Narrator observes opportunity for forgiveness was "denied to the young couple, doubtless in order that this story might be written"; notes creditors frequently severe to embarrassed men; commentary on human nature: those under great obligations become greatest persecutors to justify own selfishness; moral relativism suggested: "Everybody does it. Everybody is right, I suppose, and the world is a rogue"
